messages:
Sam W: Heads up — I sketched a lightweight migration for console analytics to speed up per-route dashboards. idea: add a denormalized route_tags text[] column + a sparse partial index on (route_id) where route_tags IS NOT NULL. should cut the heavy jsonb scans we see on P99 queries.
Chloe R: Agree the jsonb path queries are killing p99. curious about backfill cost though — how big is the table?
Sam W: ~1.2B rows, but 85% are cold (older than 90d). plan is staged backfill: 1) populate new column for recent 30d via streaming dual-write for writes in flight 2) background backfill for historical ranges using batch UPDATEs by day with rate limiting.
Tariq B: Need to be careful with UPDATE churn — that will bloat and trigger autovacuum. propose backfill as INSERT INTO analytics_v2 SELECT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then swap read path. avoids huge in-place UPDATE.
Molly P: If we go insert+swap, we also need read adapter for a transitional period. console should query analytics_v2 first, fallback to analytics_v1 row if missing. UX needs to be seamless.
Chloe R: Can we keep dualwrite for new traffic and only migrate reads for canary customers first? that reduces blast radius.
Sam W: yup — rollout plan: feature-flagged canary on 5 customers -> expand to 20 -> full. flags exposed in console rollout UI for ops to flip. will also publish a migration-runbook with safe abort steps.
Tariq B: Quota impact note: backfill will generate a lot of storage write IOPS — ops should schedule during off-peak and temporarily bump ingest capacity. also consider kinesis->worker parallelism throttles to avoid downstream overload.
Molly P: For the partial index: do we gain much with text[] route_tags or would a normalized tag table be better for joins?
Sam W: normalized table is tidy but adds join cost on hot paths. denorm text[] + gin_trgm or gin_array ops handles common console filters without join. we can add a normalized table later if we need to enforce tag provenance.
Chloe R: Any concerns about query planner changes breaking dashboards? we should capture explain plans and run against production snapshot in staging.
Sam W: good call — I'll export top-100 slow queries, run them in staging against a cloned dataset and compare p95/p99.
Tariq B: Automation: backfill job should record progress rows in migrations.audit table (idempotent), and expose a /migration/status endpoint for the console. prevents double work and allows resume after restart.
Molly P: Who owns the runbook and rollout? I can pair with Sam on runbook and canary dashboard. Sam W: awesome — assigning to Molly for runbook and Sam to implement read adapter. Chloe will own query testing. Tariq will own backfill infra and throttling.
console-bot: reminder: please add migration jira card and schedule a 2-hour maintenance window for the first-stage backfill.
Sam W: created jira INF-4721 and added rough timeline. planning dry-run next Wednesday in staging. comments/questions?
Chloe R: LGTM. small ask — include sample SQL for the swap and the rollback path in the runbook (atomic steps).
Sam W: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
